uncertainty_budget.explanation: The Indian market price of the token against the official rupee rate for a dollar. This is the bulk of the gap and it is the part everyone argues about.
No rate was published on the settlement date. Stepping back to 2026-06-25 or forward to 2026-06-29 is undetermined — Rule 206 does not say which.
A daily candle is not a price. It is a range with four printed readings and no rule choosing between them.
The retrieved pair is USDT/INR. The receipt was USDC. The figure is USDT/INR x USDC/USDT, and treating the peg as exactly 1.0000 is a further choice.

regimes.outcome: The receipt of USDC is classified as income from the transfer of a virtual digital asset, taxed at 30% under s.115BBH. The recognition date is the settlement date, June 28, 2026. The valuation method is the price that such property would ordinarily fetch on sale in the open market on the valuation date, as per Rule 57. There is a TDS obligation at 1% under s.393(1) [Table: Sl. No. 8(vi)], but it is exempt due to the threshold limit of ₹50,000. Under s.439(8), a disclosed position must be bona fide and all material facts must be disclosed.

citation.provision: Section 115BBH, Income-tax Act, 1961 — carried into the Income-tax Act, 2025

regimes.reasoning: The classification of the receipt as income from the transfer of a virtual digital asset is settled by s.115BBH, which taxes such transfers at 30%. The recognition date is the settlement date, June 28, 2026, as per the facts provided. The valuation method is determined by Rule 57, which applies the open market value on the valuation date. The TDS obligation is governed by s.393(1) [Table: Sl. No. 8(vi)], but the threshold limit of ₹50,000 exempts the payer from this obligation. Under s.439(8), a disclosed position must be bona fide and all material facts must be disclosed.
